info.title: toboggan-server
info.description: Axum WebSocket server with REST API and real-time presentation synchronization

ClientRole.description:
Which side of the projector a connection is on.

Navigation is shared state — every presenter drives the same deck — so this
is not about whose deck it is. It is about the two things a spectator must
not be able to do: move the presentation, and open a shell on the machine
hosting it.

[`Self::Audience`] is the default deliberately. A role that arrives unset,
from an older client or a hand-written frame, is the one that can do the
least.

oneOf.description:
Join the presentation. The first thing a client sends.

The server replies with [`crate::Notification::Registered`], which is
where the client learns its id and the role it was granted.

name.description: A human-readable name for this client, shown in `GET /api/clients`.

token.description:
The presenter token this client was given, if any.

A client *offers* a token; it never claims a role. The server is the
only thing that decides what a connection may do, so a client that
lies about itself gains nothing.

oneOf.description: Leave the presentation.
Heartbeat. Answered with [`crate::Notification::Pong`].
Go to the first slide.
Go to the last slide.
Go to a specific slide.

slide.description: The slide to show, as a 0-based index.

oneOf.description: Go to the next slide, skipping any reveals left on this one.
Go to the previous slide.

Reveal the next step, moving to the next slide once this one runs out.

This is what a presenter remote and the space bar send, because it walks
the whole deck rather than skipping every build.
Go back one step, moving to the previous slide once this one runs out.
Flash every other client, to get the room's attention.

Command.description:
What a client asks the server to do.

Sent over `/api/ws`, or posted to `/api/command`. The server applies the
command and broadcasts the resulting [`crate::State`] to *every* client, so
a command is a request about the shared deck rather than about the sender's
own view.

Everything except registration and the heartbeat is privileged; see
[`Command::drives_the_deck`].

oneOf.description: Nothing at all — an absent title, a slide with no notes.
Plain text, with no markup to interpret.
An HTML fragment, as produced by rendering a slide's Markdown.

alt.description:
A plain-text description, for anything that cannot show markup —
the terminal client, the stats table, a screen reader.

raw.description: The markup, ready to be placed into the document.

style.description: Classes and inline style to apply where this is rendered.

Content.description:
Anything a slide can say: its title, its body, or its speaker notes.

Use [`Self::display_text`] to ask what a piece of content *says*, rather
than matching on the variants — the variants exist so that a renderer which
can show markup gets markup, and everything else gets words.

oneOf.description: The deck moved. Broadcast to every client after every change.

seq.description:
Which change this is, counting from one.

See [`Notification::UNNUMBERED`] for what a zero means.

oneOf.description:
Something went wrong, for this client only.

Used rather than a disconnect when an audience client sends a command it
is not allowed to send: a stale tab is a mistake, not an attack.

message.description: What went wrong, in words a presenter can read.

oneOf.description: Answer to [`crate::Command::Ping`].
Flash the screen — someone pressed `b`.

The deck itself was rebuilt, so clients should re-fetch it.

Sent by the file watcher in live-reload mode.

seq.description: Which change this is, on the same counter as [`Self::State`].

state.description: Where the presentation is in the new deck.

oneOf.description:
Sent to the registering client with their assigned ID and the role the
server granted them.

The role is told rather than asked for: a client cannot know whether it
may drive the deck until the server has looked at where it connected
from, so this is where a UI learns to hide its navigation controls.

client_id.description: The id the server assigned to this connection.

role.description: What this client is allowed to do.

oneOf.description: Broadcast when a client connects
Broadcast when a client disconnects

name.description: The name it had registered under.

Notification.description:
What the server tells its clients.

Most notifications are broadcast to everyone — the deck is shared state, so
a change one client asked for is news for all of them. [`Self::Error`] and
[`Self::Registered`] go only to the client concerned.

RenderTarget.description:
Rendering targets for per-slide visibility control.

Used with `hidden_in` on a slide to exclude it from specific outputs.
An empty set means the slide is visible in all targets.

Slide.description:
One slide: what it says, how it looks, and what it is meant to cost in time.

Built by the parser from one Markdown file — [`Slide::from_markdown`] is the
constructor that keeps `body` and `body_source` consistent.

oneOf.description: Everything below the heading.

body_source.description:
Raw markdown source of the slide body, used by non-HTML exporters.

When `Some`, `body` is expected to be the rendered projection of this
source — `Slide::from_markdown` is the constructor that pairs them
consistently; ad-hoc construction must uphold that invariant.

duration.description:
Speaking time the author planned for this slide, from the front matter
`duration`.

Serialized as whole seconds so a built artifact stays readable and
round-trips; the front matter accepts either a number of seconds or a
humantime string like `"2m 30s"`.

hidden_in.description: Targets this slide should be excluded from. Empty means visible everywhere.

oneOf.description: Whether this is the cover, a section title, or an ordinary slide.

lint_disabled.description:
Lint rule ids silenced for this slide (front matter `disabled_rules` or a
`<!-- lint-disable rule-id -->` body comment). Disabling is per-slide:
diagnostics are not line-tracked, so a directive covers the whole slide.

oneOf.description:
Speaker notes — shown in the presenter view and the terminal client,
never on the projector.

quake_terminal_cwd.description:
Working directory for the `QuakeTerminal` overlay when this slide is active.
If unset, falls back to [`Talk::default_terminal_cwd`], then to the server cwd.
Resolved against [`Talk::source_dir`] when relative.

oneOf.description: Classes and inline style applied to the slide's `<section>`.

terminals.description: Embedded terminals declared by the slide, rendered side by side.

oneOf.description: The slide's heading. Empty for a slide that deliberately has none.

SlideId.description:
A type-safe identifier for slides in a presentation.

`SlideId` wraps a `usize` to provide type safety when indexing into slide collections.

SlideKind.description: What kind of slide this is, which is what decides how it is laid out.

SlidesResponse.description: The body of `GET /api/slides`: every slide in the deck.

oneOf.description: Nothing has been shown yet.
Showing a slide.

current_step.description: Which reveal within that slide is showing.

oneOf.description: Past the last slide.

current_step.description: The reveal it was left on.

State.description:
Where the presentation is: the one piece of state every client shares.

Broadcast as [`crate::Notification::State`] after every change, which is
what keeps a browser, a terminal and a phone showing the same slide.

There are exactly three states, and no pause: a deck that is not moving is
simply a `Running` state nobody is sending commands about.

Style.description: How a slide is dressed: CSS classes and an optional inline style.

classes.description: Classes applied to the slide, from the `classes` front matter key.

style.description: An inline `style` attribute, from the `style` front matter key.

TalkResponse.description:
The body of `GET /api/talk`: everything about a deck except its slides.

Carries slide *titles* rather than slides, so a client can render an outline,
a progress bar and a presenter view without pulling the whole deck — and so
the server can answer from a shared talk instead of deep-cloning every
slide's rendered HTML on every request.

date.description: The date the talk is given.

durations.description:
Planned speaking time per slide, in seconds, from each slide's
`duration` front matter. `None` where the author did not say.

Parallel to `titles`, and here rather than fetched per slide because the
presenter view needs the *whole* plan to work out whether the talk is
running early or late — one number per slide is far less than the deck.

footer.description: Footer markup, if the deck has any.

head.description: `<head>` markup, if the deck has any.

step_counts.description:
Step counts per slide, for clients that show step progress. Either
absent, or exactly as long as `titles` and read against it by index.

TerminalConfig.description:
Configuration for an embedded terminal in a slide.

Parsed from `<!-- term: path/to/cwd -->`, `<!-- term: path/to/cwd :light -->`,
`<!-- term: path/to/cwd | command -->`, or `<!-- term: path/to/cwd :light | command -->`.
Multiple terminals per slide are supported (rendered side by side).

cmd.description: Optional command to run instead of the default shell

cwd.description: Working directory for the terminal session

theme.description: Terminal color theme, defaults to dark
